J-B54.before: This is a horrible catch-22. Wounded people get lonely, and loneliness itself can kill. But the wounds that make somebody desperate for a relationship may also make them a terrible person to be in one with. People don’t only trigger each other and learn lessons. Sometimes they terrorize or kill each other.

J-B54.before: A good relationship can teach you self-love too, which is part of the problem: you may need one most when you’re least capable of creating a good one, recognizing one, or keeping it good. It depends what each of you are ready for and have the resources for. Here’s a video that can help understand the long process.
after: A good relationship can teach you self-love too, which is part of the problem: you may need one most when you’re least capable of creating a good one, recognizing one, or keeping it good. Whether you should be in one depends on what you and the other person are ready for and have the resources for. Here’s a video that can help understand the long process.

J-B217.before: That little paradise is wonderful, but it contains the seed of its own destruction. Part of why it feels like a magical wonderland is that you can suddenly stop parenting yourself now that you have someone who’s fully got your back. This makes you soft and weak, kinda like a sweet treat or heroin. It is wonderful to have their love and support, but don’t let that bring you away from your own self-love, reparenting, meditation, yoga, and other healing practices that keep you independently healthy. Otherwise, you’ll end up blaming them when you feel bad.

J-B255.before: I could teach these women about loving and reparenting their inner child, Buddhism, meditation, and other things I understood better. They could pull me into life more, show me where I was missing people, and sometimes be the skeptic when I was seeing the best in someone and missing their hidden motives.
